newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - March 11.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - March 11.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on
Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name
Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Hungary's advertising market grew by a third in 1996 to 64 billion forints ($359.5 million). Broadcast media grew at the expense of print, with television claiming a 41.4 percent share of the advertising market and radio an 8.8 percent share.
Radio's share could climb to 20 percent in 1997. (Vilaggazdasag,
March 6, 1997)

-- Outdoor advertising in the Czech Republic generated record revenues of 1.02 billion crowns ($34.6 million) in 1996, according to an estimate from IP Praha. According to reports from Strategie, billboard revenues reached 1.102 billion crowns. (Strategie, February 26-March 3)

-- The Hungarian parliament has begun debating an advertising draft bill, expected to take effect from July 1 1997, that would prohibit all media advertising of tobacco products. The advertising of alcoholic drinks would be banned from public service radio and television. (Napi Gazdasag, March 5, 1997)
-- The Czech Republic's most successful billboards in 1996 were for Magnum, Zlate Stranky yellow pages and Old Spice, according to Plakat Monitor. (Strategie, February 26-March 3)

-- The Czech Advertising Council's arbitration committee has recommended dismantling a controversial billboard ad of advertising company IP Reklama. The billboard shows three heads of a young girl, the first with a cigar, the second with a stamp on her extended tongue and the third with a symbol that stands for the female gender shaved into the back of the head. IP
claims the picture is of a sun. (Lidove Noviny, March 6)
-- The Czech ice hockey league and marketing partner Teleaxis
have agreed on a new contract guaranteeing the league 105 million crowns within three years. The contract is to be signed by the end of March. (Lidove Noviny, March 4)
-- Grey and Corporate Profiles/DDB advertising agencies have
received the lion's share of Poland's prestigious DEA awards in the 1997 competition. (Gazeta Wyborcza, March 3, 1997)

-- Poland's direct mail advertising industry is ripe for growth due to an overload of traditional advertising on the media, Ammirati Puris Lintas marketing director Coleen Cahill says. (Nowa Europe, March 3, 1997)
-- ANR AMER Nielsen Research firm is no longer publishing annual reports on company outdoor advertising expenses because few advertising agencies would reveal figures. (Media Polska, March 1997)

-- Poland's most memborable billboard advertisement for a car last November was for the Ford Mondeo, according to a survey by Mareco Poland, part of the Gallup International network. (Media Polska, March 1997)
-- Advertising annoys about 80 percent of Poles, 64 percent
consider it misleading, and only 31 percent find it informative, according to a survey by the CBOS polling institute. (Gazeta Wyborcza advertising supplement, February/March 1997)

-- About 42 percent of Poles never confirm information about an advertised product with another source before making a purchase, while 20 percent do so rarely, according to a survey by the CBOS polling institute. (Gazeta Wyborcza advertising supplement, February/March 1997)

-- Polish companies spent $19 per capita on advertising in 1996, totalling $750 million, Optimum Media's general director Jakub Bierzynski says. Television advertising costs are expected to rise 300 percent growth in the next few years, Bierzynski says. (Gazeta Wyborcza advertising supplement, February/March 1997)
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:

-- The Czech Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting issued warnings to Prima television and TV Nova for unsuitable programming. Prima television was told to modify its programme "Runaway Party," a show featuring videoclips and skits. TV Nova was cited for advertisements for erotic telephone hotlines
broadcast before 10 p.m. (Tyden, March 3)

-- Filmnet will stop broadcasting its paid channel in Poland and former subscribers will be supplied with free decorders by Canal Plus, following the merger of Canal Plus and Nethold, Filmnet's parent company. Filmnet has had 15,000 subscribers in Poland, compared to 150,000 for Canal Plus. (Gazeta Wyborcza, March 3,

-- The Czech Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting has revoked the radio broadcasting licence for Medes s.r.o., operator of Radio Rocco, for allegedly not fulfilling licence requirements. Italian-owned Radio Rocco wants to file suit against the council's decision. (Strategie, February 26 - March

-- Poland's Polsat satellite television broadcaster will launch Polsat 2, an uncoded channel showing films, programmes for children, and a Polish-language global news service. (Gazeta Wyborcza, March 3, 1997)
-- The Czech Film and Television Academy awarded a record six
Czech Lions to the film "Kolja," including best film, best director and best screenplay. (Pravo, March 3, 1997)

-- Mlada Fronta Dnes remains the Czech Republic's most-read daily newspaper. According to a survey by Amasia, Mlada Fronta is read by 21 percent of Czech's, followed by Blesk with 15 percent and Pravo with 14 percent. (Mlada Fronta Dnes, March 5,
